To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the glasma is not thermalized in the conventional sense, and it is a highly nontrivial process that leads to a hydrodynamic onset in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and LHC.

the glasma evolves toward thermal equilibrium through an intermediate stage of a nonthermal fixed point (NFP); the NFP is a nonequilibrium attractor that can be characterized as a weakly-coupling fixed point; and the NFP is the origin of the apparent thermalization of the QGP in heavy-ion collisions.

the glasma is an unstable state, and it decays into a thermalized QGP via the Landau damping of high-momentum modes, and this process occurs on a timescale ~o(1/Qs), where Qs is a typical transverse momentum of the produced particles.

there is no such thing as thermalization.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glasma evolution can be described by a set of kinetic equations for the color charge densities of the gluons.
the glasma is indeed an effective kinetic theory, which is characterized by the large gluon occupation number and strong gluon–gluon scattering cross sections.
the glasma evolution is a complicated interplay between the nonlinear Landau damping and the nonlinear gluon production, and the thermalization is a result of both.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glasma evolution is dominated by the gluon self-interaction, which is a consequence of the strong non-Abelian gauge symmetry of the underlying theory.
the glasma is not a thermalized QGP and the thermalization is not a sudden process but rather a kinetic evolution of the glasmon distribution function.
